title: Leaving Vietnam checklist for teachers (2026)
description: An 8-week plan for teachers leaving Vietnam: notice, final pay, tax finalisation before you fly, the social insurance lump sum, moving money and references.
h1: Leaving Vietnam: an 8-week checklist so you leave nothing behind
intro: Start eight weeks before you fly. If you leave before your contract ends, give written notice (at least 30 days on a 12 to 36-month contract); make sure you are paid in full within 14 working days, finalise your income tax before you leave, and claim your social insurance lump sum if you were on a contract of 12 months or more. Keep one Vietnamese bank account open for the money that arrives after you go, and take an experience letter and copies of every work permit with you.
keyPoints: To resign you give **30 days' notice** on a 12 to 36-month contract or 3 working days on a shorter one; when the contract ends the employer must settle everything within **14 working days**.

A tax-resident foreigner must **finalise income tax before leaving** Vietnam (and within 45 days of the contract ending) or authorise someone to do it. Since 1 July 2026 any overdue tax can stop a foreigner from leaving.
On a contract of 12 months or more you can claim the **social insurance lump sum** as soon as the contract ends: 2 months of average contribution salary for each year contributed.
Unused annual leave is paid out and, from 2026, is tax-free; severance (half a month's pay a year after 12 months' service) is also not taxed.
Keep a Vietnamese bank account and your phone number alive until the last payment lands: tax refunds go only to an account in your own name, and Wise cannot send đồng out of Vietnam.

blocks.text: Most of what goes wrong when teachers leave Vietnam is timing: notice given too late, tax left until the airport, a bank account closed before the refund arrives. Work backwards from your flight. Each step is explained in the sections below.

items.title: 8 weeks out: read your contract and fix your last day
items.text: Check the end date, the notice clause, your unused leave and anything promised at the end, such as a bonus or a flight. Check your lease for its notice or break clause. Decide what you will sell, ship or give away.

items.title: 6 weeks out: give notice and send HR one written list
items.text: If you are leaving before the end date, give written notice now: six weeks covers the 30 days a 12 to 36-month contract requires, with room to spare. In the same email ask HR for the date and breakdown of your final pay, your tax code (MST) and tax withholding certificates, how your tax will be finalised, when your social insurance book will be closed, and an experience letter.

items.title: 5 weeks out: order the paperwork that takes time
items.text: Ask for reference letters, get your teaching-hours log signed off, and apply for a Vietnamese police check if your next employer or country may want one. Ask your bank which documents it needs to send your savings abroad.

items.title: 4 weeks out: list big items and book the flat handover
items.text: Put furniture, appliances and your motorbike up for sale three to four weeks before you go. Book the landlord's deposit inspection for well before your last week.

items.title: 2 weeks out: settle tax and start moving money
items.text: Sign the tax-finalisation authorisation or file it yourself on eTax Mobile, and pay any balance. Start transferring savings home against your payslips and contract.

items.title: Last week: hand back, collect, sign
items.text: On your last day, hand your work permit to HR and keep a copy. Collect any originals the school holds and copies of your contracts and payslips. If someone will claim your social insurance for you, sign a certified authorisation now. Move e-wallet balances back to your bank and pay the final bills.

items.title: Departure day: two last checks
items.text: Check the eTax app for any outstanding tax. Declare cash above the limits at the airport.

items.title: After you land: watch the money come in
items.text: Final pay is due within 14 working days of the contract ending; the lump sum and any tax refund follow. Keep your Vietnamese account and SIM working until all three have arrived.

sections.title: Giving notice and getting your final pay

blocks.text: Foreign teachers are on fixed-term contracts, because a contract may not outlast the work permit, so the notice rules are simple. Under the [Labour Code 2019](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html) (Art. 35) you can resign for any reason with written notice. The 45-day period you may read about applies only to indefinite-term contracts, which foreigners cannot have.

blocks.caption: How much notice a teacher must give to resign (Labour Code 2019, Arts. 35 and 36)
rows: Not paid in full or on time, not given the agreed job or conditions, mistreated, harassed or given dishonest information
Contract simply reaches its end date
The 2019 Code sets no advance-notice period; tell the school anyway

blocks.text: Send notice by email and get a signed copy back. Leaving without the notice you owe makes the resignation unlawful: you lose severance and owe half a month's salary plus pay for the notice days you did not give, plus training costs only if you signed a written training contract (Art. 40). The Labour Code has **no provision for extra 'contract-breaking fees'** or bonds, as the [contracts guide](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teaching-contracts-in-vietnam) explains. One trap: a lawful force-majeure pay delay of up to 30 days does not give you the right to walk out without notice.
What the school owes you, and by when

When the contract ends, both sides must settle everything **within 14 working days**, or up to 30 days if the employer is closing, restructuring, merging or hit by a disaster or epidemic. The employer must also confirm your social insurance periods, return any originals it holds and give you copies of your work records if you ask ([Labour Code Art. 48](https://hethongphapluat.com/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019/khoan-3-dieu-48)).

blocks.caption: Money due when a teaching contract ends, and how it is taxed (Labour Code 2019; Decree 253/2026/ND-CP; Social Insurance Law 2024)
rows: Anyone with untaken leave (12 days a year after 12 months, pro rata before)
12+ months of regular work, contract ended by expiry, agreement or lawful resignation
Half a month's average salary (last 6 months) per year of service
Teachers enrolled on contracts of 12+ months
2 months' average contribution salary per year contributed

blocks.text: Severance is half a month's average salary for each year of service. Foreigners are outside unemployment insurance, so their whole service usually counts ([Apolat Legal](https://apolatlegal.com/paying-severance-allowance-for-foreign-employees-key-considerations-for-employers/)). It can be reduced if the employer paid you an unemployment-insurance equivalent with your salary and can prove it. Whether severance is owed when the contract and the work permit end on the same day is not settled, so ask HR in writing how they calculate it. As an illustration (our calculation), two years at an average {{vnd:40000000}} a month gives severance of about {{vnd:40000000}}.

Unused leave pay and severance are both outside income tax under [Decree 253/2026/ND-CP](https://congbaocdn.chinhphu.vn/180507251028987904/2026/7/16/469959-1784171413_v1_1784174315_signed.pdf) (Arts. 8.3(h) and 26). If the money does not arrive, send a written demand, then request mediation within **6 months** of discovering the problem; court claims must be filed within a year, and a severance dispute can go straight to court ([Labour Code, Chapter XIV](https://hethongphapluat.com/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019/chuong-14)). Employees suing for unpaid wages or severance pay [no court fees](https://ketoananpha.vn/nghi-quyet-326-2016-ubtvqh14).

sections.title: Tax finalisation before you leave Vietnam

blocks.text: If you were a tax resident, you must finalise your income tax **before you leave Vietnam** when your contract ends, or authorise an organisation or person to finalise for you; you stay responsible for any tax due ([Decree 253/2026/ND-CP](https://congbaocdn.chinhphu.vn/180507251028987904/2026/7/16/469959-1784171413_v1_1784174315_signed.pdf), Art. 50.3(c)). [Decree 252/2026/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/thue/nghi-dinh-252-2026-nd-cp-huong-dan-thi-hanh-luat-quan-ly-thue-439382-d1.html) (Art. 10.5.d) sets the deadline: before you exit, and no later than 45 days after the labour contract ends.

Non-residents pay a flat 20% that is final on each payment, so there is nothing to finalise; check the residency test first, because leases adding up to 183 days in the tax year can make you resident. If you leave in 2026, finalising is the only way to recover tax over-withheld under the old scale from January to June, and since 1 July 2026 a foreigner with overdue tax can be [temporarily barred from leaving Vietnam](https://thoibaotaichinhvietnam.vn/cac-truong-hop-tam-hoan-xuat-canh-do-no-thue-200118.html), so finalise and pay weeks before your flight. The eTax steps, who can authorise the school to finalise, and the residency rules are in the [income tax guide](/teach-in-vietnam/personal-income-tax-for-teachers-in-vietnam#leaving-vietnam-tax).

sections.title: Claiming your social insurance lump sum

blocks.text: Since 1 July 2025 foreign employees on contracts of 12 months or more pay 9.5% of salary into compulsory social and health insurance, and the employer pays 20.5%. When you leave you can claim a one-time lump sum. Under the [Social Insurance Law 2024](https://english.luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/law-41-2024-qh15-on-social-insurance-360809-d1.html) (Art. 70), a foreign contributor can claim when the labour contract ends or the work permit expires and is not renewed, with **no 12-month waiting period**. Teachers on contracts under 12 months are outside the scheme and have no lump sum to claim.

The lump sum is **2 months of average contribution salary for each year** contributed from 2014 (1.5 months for years before 2014). For less than a year, it is what was contributed, capped at 2 months.

Before your last day, ask HR for your contribution record and to close your social insurance book promptly. If you will leave before you can file, sign a certified written authorisation in Vietnam before you fly, because one signed abroad needs extra certification. The documents, where to file, processing times and whether the lump sum is taxed are in the [social insurance guide](/teach-in-vietnam/social-and-health-insurance-for-foreign-teachers-in-vietnam#lump-sum).

sections.title: Closing accounts and moving your money home

blocks.text: Do not close your Vietnamese bank account until your final pay, the lump sum and any tax refund have all arrived. **Tax refunds go only to a bank account in your own name** ([Forvis Mazars eTax guide](https://www.forvismazars.com/vn/en/insights/vietnam-updates/thought-catalysts/step-by-step-guide-pit-finalization-etax-mobile)). Keep your Vietnamese phone number working too, because your banking app runs on it; the [SIM and eSIM guide](/esim-vietnam-guide) explains keeping a number.

items: Send savings home through a bank. Resident foreigners may send salary abroad; if you were paid in đồng, you buy foreign currency at a licensed bank first ([Circular 16/2014/TT-NHNN](https://caselaw.vn/van-ban-phap-luat/264720-thong-tu-16-2014-tt-nhnn-huong-dan-su-dung-tai-khoan-ngoai-te-tai-khoan-dong-viet-nam-cua-nguoi-cu-tru-nguoi-khong-cu-tru-tai-ngan-hang-duoc-phep-do-thong-doc-ngan-hang-nha-nuoc-viet-nam-ban-hanh)).

Banks send a foreigner's income abroad only up to the documented value of legal income, so bring your passport, labour contract, payslips or statements, work permit and tax documents ([PVcomBank](https://www.pvcombank.com.vn/san-pham/ca-nhan/chuyen-tien-quoc-te/chuyen-thu-nhap-hop-phap-cua-ca-nhan-nguoi-nuoc-ngoai)). PVcomBank, for one, lets an authorised person make the transfer, which helps once you have left; ask your bank what it accepts.
[Wise cannot send đồng out of Vietnam](https://www.wise.com/help/articles/2571907/what-currencies-can-i-send-to-and-from); it only accepts đồng as a currency to send into the country.
Online transfers over {{vnd:10000000}} each, or once the day's total passes {{vnd:20000000}}, need face or fingerprint authentication, so test it before you go.

If the passport your bank holds on file expires, banks suspend payments and withdrawals on every channel until it is updated ([Vietcombank notice](https://www.vietcombank.com.vn/vi-VN/Trang-thong-tin-dien-tu/Articles/2024/11/07/20241107_VCB-TCBC-vv-Cap-nhat-STH-va-GTTT-de-khong-bi-gian-doan-giao-dich-tu-01012025)). Update it before you leave if a new passport is due.

Empty your e-wallets back into your bank account: cash withdrawals from e-wallets have been banned since 5 November 2025 ([Circular 41/2025/TT-NHNN](https://luatvietnam.vn/linh-vuc-khac/tong-hop-diem-moi-thong-tu-41-2025-tt-nhnn-ve-vi-dien-tu-883-106022-article.html)).

blocks.text: Carrying cash out is the riskiest route. Foreign cash above US$5,000, or the equivalent, must be declared at the border. So must đồng in cash above {{vnd:15000000}}, and 300 g or more of gold. From 1 July 2026 failing to declare when leaving can be fined up to {{vnd:50000000}}, and at {{vnd:100000000}} or more of undeclared value criminal liability is possible ([Decree 169/2026/ND-CP](https://hatinh.gov.vn/vi/bai-viet/khai-bao-khong-trung-thuc-ve-ngoai-te-vang-khi-xuat-nhap-canh-co-the-bi-phat-den-50-trieu-dong)). The [banking guide](/teach-in-vietnam/banking-and-sending-money-home-from-vietnam) covers transfers in detail.

sections.title: Selling up and handing back your flat

blocks.text: Our [guide to selling up before you leave Vietnam](/selling-up-before-you-leave-vietnam) covers the selling itself. For teachers the timing is what matters: list furniture, appliances and a motorbike three to four weeks before departure, which leaves time for buyers who want to view and haggle. eno.vn is a free classifieds marketplace, so you can list there alongside Facebook groups and Chợ Tốt. Sell a motorbike with a proper registration transfer instead of simply handing over the registration card, and return a rented bike on time ([renting a motorbike](/motorbike-rental-ho-chi-minh-city)).

Give your landlord the notice your lease asks for and book the deposit inspection well before your last week, so any dispute is settled while you are still in the city. Breaking a 12-month lease early commonly costs the whole deposit unless the lease has a break clause. The [rental deposit guide](/rental-deposit-vietnam) explains how to get it back.

sections.title: References and documents to take with you

blocks.text: The papers you collect in your last week are hard to get once you are gone, and your next job will ask for them.

items: **An experience letter from each employer**: signed and stamped on letterhead, stating your job title, start and end dates and whether you were full-time. Employers abroad and examining bodies use it to check your experience.

**Copies of every Vietnamese work permit and contract.** If you come back to work in Vietnam, [earlier Vietnamese work permits](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers) are how your Vietnamese experience is proved under [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html) (Art. 19.3). Hand any permit card to HR when you leave: the employer must return the permit to the authority within 15 days.

**Your teaching-hours log**, signed off where possible. Cambridge asks speaking examiners for teaching experience ideally equivalent to at least [1,800 hours](https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/teaching-english/professional-development/become-a-cambridge-english-examiner/), so hours are worth more than a vague 'two years'.
**Your payslips, tax certificates and social insurance record**, for your home tax return and for the bank.
**Any originals the school holds.** An employer may not keep your passport, degree or certificates, and must return them when you leave.

blocks.text: If your next employer or country may want a Vietnamese police check (Phiếu lý lịch tư pháp), get it before you leave. Foreigners who have lived in Vietnam can request their own, in person or by post. In Ho Chi Minh City the police take applications at three counters, including 161 Nguyễn Du in Bến Thành ward ([Tuổi Trẻ](https://tuoitre.vn/cong-an-tp-hcm-thay-doi-dia-diem-tiep-nhan-va-tra-ket-qua-ly-lich-tu-phap-20260213171448319.htm)). It costs {{vnd:200000}} ([Ministry of Public Security](https://dichvucong.bocongan.gov.vn/bocongan/bothutuc/tthc?matt=61555)) and takes 5 working days, or up to 15 if checks are needed ([Government portal](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/tu-1-7-thoi-han-cap-phieu-ly-lich-tu-phap-5-ngay-lam-viec-119260403092607993.htm)). The [criminal record check guide](/teach-in-vietnam/criminal-record-check-for-a-vietnam-work-permit) covers the rest.

Before you go, help the next teacher: if you worked or interviewed at a Ho Chi Minh City school, you can vote and write a review in [the school directory](/schools), where a moderator reads reviews before they appear. If you are moving into examining, training or management rather than out of teaching, the [career paths guide](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-career-path-in-vietnam) sets out what each step asks for.

faqs.q: Does my school have to give me notice when my fixed-term contract simply ends?
faqs.a: The Labour Code 2019 sets no advance-notice period before a fixed-term contract expires. Notice periods apply when either side ends the contract early: 30 days on a 12 to 36-month contract, 3 working days on a shorter one.

faqs.q: I was on a 6-month contract. Do I get any social insurance back?
faqs.a: No. Compulsory social insurance for foreigners applies only to contracts of 12 months or more, so a shorter contract means no contributions and no lump sum to claim.

faqs.q: I was a non-resident for tax. Do I still need to finalise before leaving?
faqs.a: No. Non-residents pay a flat 20% on Vietnamese salary, and that tax is final on each payment, so there is no annual finalisation. Check you really were non-resident: leases adding up to 183 days in the tax year also make you resident unless you can prove tax residence elsewhere.

faqs.q: Can my school charge me a fee for leaving early?
faqs.a: The Labour Code sets what you owe for quitting without the required notice: half a month's salary plus pay for the missing notice days, and training costs only under a written training contract. It has no provision for other exit fees, bonds or deposits, and deposits are banned outright.

faqs.q: Will my embassy help if my school does not pay my final salary?
faqs.a: Embassies do not resolve employment disputes; they give guidance and lists of local lawyers. The legal route is to request a labour mediator within 6 months, then go to arbitration or a regional court; court claims must be filed within a year, and wage claims carry no court fees.
